topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, themes, and core learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer development, cellular differentiation, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations leading to the breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, including the challenges of modeling this in vitro.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the pathological differences between benign and malignant neoplasms, focusing on basement membrane invasion, metastatic dissemination, and the stepwise progression from precursor lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and pathophysiological causes of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the standardized conventions for naming tumors across tissue lineages and describe the physiological mechanisms through which local and metastatic tumors produce clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across human populations and diverse animal taxa, illustrating that neoplasia is a fundamental vulnerability of multicellular life.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles of early clinical detection and compare the diagnostic efficacy and histological basis of screening approaches across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and instructions for upcoming practicals and lectures.
